reasons: The cited clause (Section 2.1) is squarely the rule's walk-away scenario: a three-year, USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay obligation on Customer with express denial of reduction or termination rights, so the 'deviation' status is correct and directionally against us.

The redline reaches the preferred position (no minimum purchase/take-or-pay/volume commitment; payment only for Services used or ordered), which is the playbook's first-choice outcome and is internally consistent with the fee-for-usage framing.

The changed-character ratio failure is expected and acceptable here: the entire operative obligation had to be replaced, and a bare deletion would leave a gap; the substituted sentence is short and adds no new burdens on Customer.

The comment is accurate, in the required tone and prefix, explains what was removed and why, notes the internal conflict with the Section 12.3 no-minimum acknowledgement, and offers the exact fallback (12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, true-up not penalty).
